title: Iran war costing each US household ~$2,000: Moodys
summary: CNN segment (Oct 2026) on Moody's estimate that the Iran war has cost households about $2,000 via energy, borrowing costs and military spending, plus a partisan panel on affordability before the midterms.

assertions.quote: Energy alone is $1,100 per family according to Moody's.
inflation is up, bond rates are up, the Fed is raising interest rates for the first time in three years.

verdicts.note: An oil shock lifts inflation expectations and Treasury yields, which feed mortgage and card rates; the size rests on Moody's model, which is not independently checked here.

assertions.quote: They've responded by cutting some of their cheaper flights, by raising baggage fees and lifting airfare.

verdicts.note: Fuel is 20 to 30 percent of airline costs and carriers routinely raise fares and cut capacity when it spikes, as in 2008 and 2022.

Airline fares rose 22.4% in the 12 months to September 2026 (1.2% in the month) while fuel oil rose 74.2% and energy 20.4%, consistent with fuel costs passing into fares; the release reports the co-movement without attributing it.

assertions.quote: once we get through the conflict with Iran, the price of gas goes down, the price of goods therefore goes down.
Wage growth that isn't quite keeping up with inflation.

verdicts.note: With CPI at 3.7 percent and average hourly earnings growing about 3 percent in 2026, real wages have slipped for several months, reversing 2024-2025 gains.

assertions.quote: more people working in wage growth right now. So those are some good things. They still have to address affordability.

verdicts.note: 2026 shows low unemployment and record equity prices alongside wages trailing a 3.7 percent CPI, as 2021-2022 did.

assertions.quote: gas has never been above $4 a gallon as many times in a calendar year as this year.

verdicts.note: AAA data back to 2000 show only 2008 and 2022 with sustained 4 dollar gas, and 2026 passed the 2022 count of 158 days by October.

Counting weekly national-average readings at or above 4.00 as a proxy for days, 2026 has 24 such weeks through 10/12 (Apr-May 8, Jun 3, Jul 2, Aug 5, Sep 4, Oct 2) against 23 in all of 2022 (Mar 7 to Aug 8) and 7 in 2008, so 2026 already exceeds every prior year with eleven weeks still to run; the national weekly average is a proxy, not a daily count.
